deal_summary: The customer requested a conveyor and printer solution, compared the proposed mechanism with its director, agreed to a revised technical option and 50/20/30 payment terms, and proceeded to a signed contract and invoice. The buyer's legal review raised delivery-risk clauses; the seller explained its pickup/carrier arrangement and exchanged revised documents. At the last event, payment was expected but not confirmed in the view. [evidence: 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 12, 13]

customer_need.summary: A roughly two-meter conveyor with inkjet marking for containers, with reliable spacing/sensing so the print is not smeared; the buyer's director asked whether a divider was needed and wanted a sample-based demonstration. [evidence: 1, 5]

deal_dynamics.early: The buyer prioritized finding a workable technical solution over price, provided container photos, and requested a conveyor/printer quote. [evidence: 0, 1]
deal_dynamics.middle: The buyer's director reviewed the proposal and raised concerns about container separation and print reliability. The seller checked with production, priced a divider as an option, shared videos, and discussed 50/20/30 terms. [evidence: 3, 4, 5, 6]
deal_dynamics.late: The buyer approved preparing a contract as an individual entrepreneur, supplied or discussed sample containers, and returned a signed contract. Contract review then focused on delivery responsibility; the seller rejected two delivery clauses under its pickup/carrier model, sent an editable contract, and later countersigned and sent an invoice. [evidence: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13]

Said the director was leaning toward the seller's option, then approved starting contract preparation. [evidence: 3, 7]
Returned signed paperwork and continued coordinating payment and document format. [evidence: 11, 12, 13]
negative_signals: The director required additional assurance about spacing, sensing, print quality, and divider operation before settling the design. [evidence: 5]

customer_behavior.initiative: The customer asked about the separation mechanism, involved its director, requested video/sample validation, supplied a counter-protocol on delivery, and followed up on the signed documents and payment. [evidence: 1, 5, 7, 9, 12, 13]
customer_behavior.decision_process: A director approved the technical/commercial path; the contract was to be purchased by an individual entrepreneur, with legal review and EDO/paper signature options. [evidence: 3, 7, 9, 12]

strong_actions: Obtained a production-backed solution and explained the conveyor, side supports, sensor, and optional divider. [evidence: 1, 5, 6]
Provided a revised offer, video, and structured payment terms after the director's questions. [evidence: 5, 6]
Prepared a contract for the buyer's legal review, sent it in Word when requested, and returned the seller-signed copy with an invoice. [evidence: 7, 10, 11]
weak_actions: The initial quote did not resolve the buyer's key concern about closely spaced containers; a sample run or clear separation diagram was needed after the director raised it. [evidence: 1, 5]
The offer/contract email was not received promptly and had to be re-sent through Telegram; the customer also later could not find the contract attachment and requested a Word copy. [evidence: 2, 10]
Pickup/carrier responsibility was clarified only after legal review, leaving two delivery clauses unresolved. [evidence: 9]
manager_behavior.follow_up_quality: Prompt and persistent, using calls, email, Telegram, production questions, and repeat document delivery. The customer still had a legal/signature-format question and payment timing remained unconfirmed at the endpoint. [evidence: 2, 5, 6, 10, 12, 13]
manager_behavior.next_step_control: The seller sent a signed contract and invoice; the immediate next step was the buyer's payment and confirmation of signature channel. No payment proof or later completion appears in the view. [evidence: 11, 12, 13]
